pr_body:
This changes the way that ExtensionData is gathered and assigned so that properties are added and assigned before finishing parsing an object.

This works for the following dictionary types
- `Dictionary<,>`
- `SortedDictionary<,>`
- `IDictionary<,>`
- `IReadOnlyDictionary<,>`
- `ImmutableDictionary<,>`
- `ImmutableSortedDictionary<,>`
- `IImmutableDictionary<,>`
- `ConcurrentDictionary<,>`

closes #31645

issue_context.title: Support using any dictionary as JsonExtensionData
issue_context.body:
IMHO, `IReadOnlyDictionary` should work identical to `IDictionary` when using with  `JsonExtensionData` attribute.

```cs
[JsonExtensionData]
public IReadOnlyDictionary<string, JsonElement> Payload { get; set; }
```

Currently it fails with error:
> System.InvalidOperationException: The data extension property 'Payload' does not match the required signature of IDictionary<string, JsonElement> or IDictionary<string, object>.

This is analogous to collection properties which can be defined as `List<T>`, `IList<T>` or `IReadOnlyList<T>` etc.
comments:

> Hopefully that ramble makes some sense 😄

@Romanx, yes it does 😄

> Adding a dictionary to the JsonPropertyInfo for the ExtensionData

`JsonPropertyInfo` and `JsonClassInfo` are used to cache type metadata & to set/get properties, and can be used by multiple threads at the same time. They thus can't store any (de)serialization specific state as this won't be thread-safe.

`ReadStackFrame` would be a good place to add a new dictionary property to temporarily hold extension data, as each instance is specific to the deserialization of one object.

> converting before returning the final result by exposing the collection conversion from the JsonConverter

After deserialization, logic similar to what you've seen in the dictionary converters can be used to instantiate and populate the desired dictionary type. I expect this conversion to take place in the converter for the object, not one of the dictionary converters.

review_comments:
We need to test the behavior (serialization & deserialization) when a converter is used:

- a converter for each dictionary added at runtime through JsonSerializerOptions.Converter.Add
- a converter added on the extension dictionary property with `JsonConverterAttribute`
- a converter placed on a custom dictionary type (e.g. some `public class MyDictionary : IReadOnlyDictionary<string, JsonElement>`) with `JsonConverterAttribute`.

The test for converters are handled separately from these additional tests such as the test `CustomObjectConverterInExtensionProperty`. We could add more tests for the specific types here but that wouldn't be testing any new codepaths since there's no specific logic for converters changed here so these verify we didn't break anything existing
What's the behavior with non-generic dictionaries? We need tests for types supported by each dictionary converter.
We need negative tests where the generic dictionary types are supported, but they key type is not `string` and/or the value type is not `object` or `JsonElement`.

The negative tests we have as `ExtensionProperty_InvalidDictionary` but we can add tests for the specific types if you think that's worthwhile.

Do you mean non generic dictionaries like `IDictionary`? I don't think that will work since it needs to match either `<string, object>` or `<string, JsonElement>`.
Let's add tests where the object is deserialized with a parameterized constructor.
Please add JSON properties to the above tests and verify the results of the deserialization operations.

I think the tests above are to verify that no exceptions are thrown when the extension data isn't used but does when it tries to deserialize into it. I removed these two since they're no longer accurate and it does serialize

The reflection being added to this method will occur during deserialization (as opposed to during the serializer's warm-up, when `JsonClassInfo`s and `JsonPropertyInfo`s are created), and will lead to bad throughput performance.

I'll come back to this in a follow-up review, but I think the type metadata being retrieved here can be cached on the `JsonClassInfo` for the dictionary type during warm-up.
